title: Trajectory-aware kernel dispatch & safety playbook for mixed-length models
creator: Priya Rao
description: Problem: We observe tail latency regressions and cost spikes when heterogeneous workloads (short chat, long document summarization, and occasional long-code generations) hit the runtime. Existing kernel selection is primarily static or single-step heuristic based on architecture and a coarse seqlen bucket. This ticket scopes a pragmatic, production-safe feature set to make per-request kernel dispatch trajectory-aware: using lightweight per-request warm probes, a compact per-model microvariant registry (microvariants are kernel+layout+quantization recipes), and an automated safety rollback circuit. Goals: 1) reduce 95/99 latency tails for mixed workloads, 2) avoid expensive blind warmstarts that increase cost, 3) enable gradual rollout with canary metrics and automated fallback to conservative kernel variants.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New dispatch path implemented and behind a runtime flag. 2) End-to-end benchmarks show >=15% reduction in p99 latency for mixed workloads in synthetic trace with realistic seqlen histogram while CPU/GPU utilization remains within baseline. 3) Canary rollout with automated rollback triggers (latency SLA breach, error rate, cost delta) defined and validated. 4) No user-visible correctness regressions (outputs match baseline within tolerance) across 3 representative models. 5) Documentation and console controls added (toggle, telemetry, debug trace).
decisions: Adopt a two-phase dispatch: lightweight probe (1-2 tokens) + steady-state route, rather than single-shot seqlen histogram routing.
Represent kernel choices as immutable microvariants (id, op-layout, quant-level, perf-prior) to simplify rollout and telemetry.
Use a bounded budget for probes (max 5% of requests can trigger extended probes) and fall back to conservative variant on budget exhaustion.
Telemetry will compute per-microvariant RL metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, cost-per-token, error-rate; retention policy 30d for rollout decisions.
Safety circuit triggers: p99 increase > 20% over baseline OR error-rate increase > 0.5% OR unexpected memory OOMs -> immediate rollback to previous microvariant set.
Will gate release behind feature flag and rollout via per-customer and per-cluster canaries; Dedicated customers can opt-in via console.
Quantized fallback strategy: when choosing microvariants for long sequences, prefer microvariants with established KV-warmstart patterns to avoid decode stalls.
No change to public API; internal routing decisions only.
updates: 2026-02-05 Priya Rao: Kickoff—aligned with PM (Leah) and Observability team. Collected representative traces from prod (chat, document, code).

2026-02-12 Marco Hernandez: Prototype probe instrumentation implemented in local runtime branch. Probe = first 2 decode steps on candidate microvariant; captures latency and KV hit behavior. Added probe budget counter to per-cluster config.
2026-02-18 SRE (Anika): Injected synthetic spikes on canary cluster; observed unstable behavior when probe rate >8% — reduced default probe cap to 5% and added rate-smoothing token-bucket.

2026-02-24 Benchmarks: Synthetic trace A (mix: 60% short chat, 30% medium doc, 10% long code) shows p99 drop 18% on A100 with microvariant routing vs baseline static selector. p50 unchanged. Cost delta +3% before optimizing batching window.
2026-03-02 Design review: Console UI mockups approved—toggle, probe budget, canary cohort selector, and timeline with rollback snapshot.
2026-03-07 Marco: Implemented canary guardrails and automatic rollback hook. Hook posts incident to #runtime-canary and flips feature flag when thresholds exceeded.
2026-03-10 QA: Ran correctness suite for base models (gpt-mini, long-summarizer, codegen-6B). No functional divergence beyond acceptable BLEU/ROUGE drift (<=0.6%).
2026-03-12 Observability: Hooked microvariant telemetry into Console; dashboards for per-model microvariant latency, cost-per-token, KB cache hit rate. Preparing canary rollout next week.
Next: Coordinate with Dedicated infra to schedule canary on 2026-03-18. Follow-up ticket for autoscaling integration will be created after initial canary.
test_plan: 1) Synthetic workload runner: replay 24h of anonymized traffic with seqlen distribution; compare p50/p95/p99 and cost. 2) Stress test: bursty arrival patterns and probe rate stress. 3) Regression suite for correctness across sampling seeds and RNG. 4) A/B canary with 1% then 10% then 50% traffic with automated rollback after threshold violations. 5) Dedicated customer pilot with opt-in SLA monitoring.
risks: 1) Probing can amplify latency for some workloads if not budgeted; mitigation: conservative default probe cap, token-bucket smoothing. 2) Telemetry lag could cause late rollbacks; mitigation: real-time metric ingestion for canaries and fast evaluation windows. 3) Interaction with batching may reduce probe signal quality; mitigation: probe scheduling at pre-batch boundary and logging of batch composition. 4) Edge cases with KV cache warm-starts for long-context models — plan to include warmstart-aware microvariants and conservative heuristics.
